title: Bolder hand — choose the visual world
question: The bolder roll dealt the Daylight Section first. Keep it, take the Night-Flight Six-Pack (which beat the leader on both axes), an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Daylight Section
options.lineage: architectural daylight sections: sun paths, limewash rooms, ruled drawings
options.thesis: The portfolio is a building cut in continuous section — every project a room, the sunbeam's position marking the featured work and the "now" of your career.
options.viewport: A long continuous section fills the hero: rooms (projects) cut in charcoal poche on limewash, a gold sunbeam that has reached the featured room's door, and a tabular time stamp marking the moment.

raised.raise: The visitor is a small figure crossing the section — pointer presence at warm human scale inside the architecture.
The active room renders fully resolved while rooms behind it drift a shade soft — focus reads as depth, not decoration.
Everything snaps to the ruled section grid at every size — integer stacking, nothing off-grid on any viewport.

options.risk: The building metaphor is abstract: without strong copy it reads as architecture, not engineering — every room must be filled with software's actual artifacts, screens, schemas, and diagrams.

options.label: The Night-Flight Six-Pack
options.lineage: a small aircraft's night instrument six-pack
options.thesis: Six luminous instruments on matte black, each owning one truth — and the cross-check sweep is exactly how a visitor validates you.
options.viewport: The hero is a six-pack of round gauges: white aviation numerals and tick scales, terse placard caps beneath, needles at rest — except one, the featured project's, beginning a slow damped sweep, the page's only motion.
options.case: Beats the leader on both axes: the instrument cross-check maps precisely to how a hiring manager or client validates an engineer, and "systems that hold trust through cloud" is the backend promise.
options.risk: The aviation metaphor must stay on the reliability idea — if it becomes literal cockpits it misleads; and a dark instrument panel must not tip into the dark-console rut.

options.label: The Modular Identity
options.lineage: a modular graphic identity system of colored bars over photography
options.thesis: Projects as saturated color bands snapping over real photographic panels; the category filter is a color-band, the featured project the bar that sits forward.
options.viewport: A staggered stack of saturated bars over a photographic panel; the featured project's bar snaps forward with a parallax shift as the photo layer recedes.
options.case: Holds product clarity — color-band navigation is unmistakable — but reads as a design studio, which blurs the backend identity.
options.risk: The loud palette fights the brief's "subtle, polished, functional" bar; the block grammar must carry the system while the products' content carries the volume.

options.label: The category standard
options.thesis: What this category ships — dark hero, code window, card grid, tech tags — executed impeccably.
options.viewport: The arrangement every developer-portfolio visitor expects, at full craft.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.

options.label: The Indoor Weather Sun
options.lineage: an indoor weather sun in a hazed hall
options.thesis: One vast amber horizon, mirrored ceiling, silhouettes lying in the haze — the visitor walks the long axis toward the half-sun.
options.case: Atmosphere over information: monofrequency amber fails legibility and contrast for a content-heavy portfolio, and the scene carries no engineering claim.
options.kept: The visitor as a small figure crossing the long axis — donated to the leader as pointer presence.

options.label: The Benday Comic Page
options.lineage: silver-age four-color comic pages on pulp
options.thesis: A six-panel comic grid: projects as panels, the featured project as the splash the story earns, misregistration as the house texture.
options.case: Playful pulp misreads as hobbyist, and the misregistration gimmick fights the credibility a business audience needs.
options.kept: The active panel registers clean while idle panels drift half-dot off — donated to the leader as resolved-versus-soft focus.

options.label: The Arcade CRT
options.thesis: A 240-line pixel playfield with phosphor bloom: projects as tile rooms, palette laws encoding status, scanlines doing half the shading.
options.case: The game-like aesthetic the brief bans outright, and it points at game dev rather than the backend identity.
options.kept: Integer grid discipline — everything snaps to the tile grid at every size — donated to the leader as its responsive law.
